plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: A perennial with dense, layered flower heads in many forms, from pompons to spiders. It is one of the last garden flowers to bloom in the Northern Hemisphere and tolerates light frosts. Its short-day flowering response ties its bloom time to lengthening nights.
plants.location: Cultivated worldwide, especially East Asia, Europe, and North America
plants.funFact: In Japan the chrysanthemum is the emblem of the Imperial family, and the Chrysanthemum Throne is named after it. Chrysanthemums are also traditionally used to honor the dead in parts of Europe, where they are placed on graves around All Saints' Day.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A large deciduous to semi-evergreen tree with fern-like leaves that bursts into panicles of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere, it blooms in late spring, covering streets and parks with purple carpets of fallen blossoms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring (October to December in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in South Africa, Australia, and Argentina
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, which is nicknamed the Jacaranda City, there are tens of thousands of jacaranda trees. Students traditionally say that if a jacaranda blossom falls on your head, you will pass your exams.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark leaves and fragrant, delicate flowers that open in late autumn when most other plants have finished blooming. It is more sun tolerant and earlier flowering than the common camellia, and its petals tend to shatter and drop.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to early winter (October to December)
plants.location: Native to Japan; grown in the southeastern United States, Europe, and Australia
plants.funFact: Oil pressed from sasanqua seeds is used in Japan for cooking, hair care, and polishing traditional tools and blades.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A woody shrub bearing the largest flower head in the Protea genus, with a bowl of silky bracts around a center of tiny true flowers. It thrives in the nutrient-poor soils of the fynbos region and is pollinated by beetles, and also by birds and small mammals.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to summer in the Southern Hemisphere, with flowering from September to January
plants.location: Western and Southern Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: The king protea is the national flower of South Africa, and the genus is named after Proteus, the Greek god who could change his shape.
